title: SSE epoch synchronizer, semantic delimiters, and reconnect policy for streaming outputs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We observe client-visible corruption or duplicate function-call/JSON fragments when a streaming connection is interrupted during a model rollout or runtime warm-up. Existing chunk IDs are useful for resume but don't convey epoch/rollout boundaries; clients rejoining during a model replacement can accept partial structured output that is incompatible with later tokens. Goal: introduce an 'epoch synchronizer' and explicit semantic delimiters to make reconnect behavior deterministic, preserve function-call atomicity, and support backward compatibility with older SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits an opaque epoch token in the SSE handshake and includes epoch tag on each chunk; token changes when model instance set or runtime semantics change.
Chunks include an optional semantic delimiter flag (DELIM_START / DELIM_END) to mark function-call or JSON object boundaries; clients can use delimiters to avoid emitting partial structured outputs.

Reconnect path: when a client reconnects and presents last-seen chunk id + epoch token, server can determine whether it's safe to resume, instruct client to resume, or instruct client to discard unfinished semantic block and start fresh.

Compatibility shim: older clients that do not send epoch tokens can still resume using chunk id but will be shown a deprecation header and a best-effort resume; automated migration metrics are collected.

Automated unit+integration tests validate: normal resume, resume across epoch change (should produce discard-and-restart semantics for in-flight structured objects), and multiplexed client scenarios where multiple logical streams share a connection.
Observability: tracing spans and metrics are emitted for epoch transitions, resume decisions (allowed/resync/discard), and percentage of resumes that required semantic discard.
Rollout plan documented and a feature flag exists to disable epoch-checking for troubleshooting; feature enabled by default for new regions in api-2025.03 release.
Performance overhead is measured and kept below 2% p50 latency increase for standard streaming requests.
Design review approved by Design (Lina Park) and PM (Jonah Blake).
updates: 2025-03-05 — Ticket created after a customer support incident where a function-call output was truncated across a reconnect during model swap. Initial triage by Ava Chen.

2025-03-07 — Spike completed: prototype epoch token in handshake (HTTP SSE 'X-Redwood-Epoch' header) and chunk annotate prototype implemented in runtime; microbenchmarks showed ~0.8% p50 overhead. — Diego Ramos

2025-03-10 — Design sync: agreed on two delimiter markers (DELIM_START / DELIM_END) and a third optional marker DELIM_ABORT to indicate server-initiated abort of in-flight block. Lina Park left UX notes about client SDK surface for re-emitting partial blocks.

2025-03-12 — Security review kickoff: we flagged potential information exposure in epoch token (it must be opaque). Security requested HSM-backed signing only for control-plane metadata; decided epoch tokens remain opaque random IDs with short TTLs. — Security (@Marco Singh)

2025-03-14 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — implements epoch header + chunk-tagging and compatibility shim for legacy clients. Integration tests added for resume semantics.

2025-03-16 — Performance regression testing: load test 20k concurrent streaming sessions; latency impact within acceptable range; some amplification on very short streams observed. Mitigation: batch epoch checks for short-lived connections (heuristic). — Diego Ramos

2025-03-18 — PM review: added telemetry dashboard widget spec (datadog link in PR) to track resume-decisions and epoch churn. Also defined rollback criteria (if >1% of resumes result in semantic discard within first 24h, rollout will be paused). — Jonah Blake
2025-03-20 — Code review notes from Eng on preserving idempotency of chunk IDs across restarts; added deterministic mapping tests and a follow-up ticket for KV cache cleanup behavior (ENG-7762520).
comments: Lina Park (Design): We need to ensure that SDKs surface a clear 'onPartialStructuredOutput' callback so product teams can decide whether to buffer or render. Also request copy for deprecation header for older clients.
Marco Singh (Security): Confirmed epoch tokens must not leak internal node identifiers. Use opaque nonce with rotation rather than signed node metadata.
Jonah Blake (PM): Prioritize rollout to low-risk customers first (internal dogfood → beta customers) and instrument with feature flag and monitoring.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch header encoding/decoding
Integration tests: resume within same epoch (expect exact resume), resume across epoch (expect server instructs discard-and-restart for active semantic block)
Chaos test: interrupt streams during function-call boundary; assert no malformed JSON emitted to client-facing logs
Compatibility tests: confirm older SDKs can resume by chunk id and receive deprecation header
Load test: ensure <2% p50 latency overhead at production traffic mix
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'epoch-sync' flag in control plane
Phase 1: internal dogfood (1% of sessions) for 48h
Phase 2: rollout to beta customers (10%) with curator monitoring for resume-discard rate
Phase 3: full rollout if thresholds met, otherwise rollback and collect more diagnostics
follow_up_tasks: ENG-7762520 — KV cache cleanup semantics when epoch changes
ENG-7762531 — SDK changes for onPartialStructuredOutput and deprecation header handling
ENG-7762600 — Add Datadog dashboard and alert (resume-discard-rate > 1%)
